item.title: Can Black Soldier Fly Larvae Tackle the Manure and Antibiotic Resistance Problems in our Food System?
item.description: The insects show promise in turning livestock waste into more sustainable fertilizer and by reducing antibiotic-resistant bacteria, but how well that’ll work in the real world is unclear.

item.title: Ten Million Tons of Manure In California Are Unaccounted for, New Report Shows
item.description: Stanford researchers found serious loopholes in factory farm regulation — and it’s not just in California.

item.title: North Carolina Created Complaint Systems for Its Factory Farms. They Don’t Work Very Well.
item.description: The state has only 14 inspectors for thousands of hog, poultry and cattle farms known as concentrated animal feeding operations, or CAFOs.

item.title: In an Era of Mega-Farms, These Schools Still Serve (Some) Locally Grown Food
item.description: A Minnesota school district is sourcing food from small regional farms, channeling public dollars back into communities squeezed by agricultural consolidation.

item.title: TB-Infected Cow in Michigan Discovered Beyond High-Risk Zone
item.description: A new bovine tuberculosis case shows that the disease, long thought largely eradicated, persists despite years of statewide efforts.

item.title: New Study Shows Strong Link Between Industrialized Agriculture and Declining Bird Populations
item.description: Pesticides, fertilizers and habitat destruction are the likely culprits.

item.title: Beagles Are Still Bred on Farms for Testing and Research, an Open Rescue Reveals
item.description: Authorities say several dozen animal rights activists broke into a facility in Blue Mounds, Wisconsin on March 15.

item.title: How the Humble Hornwort Could Supercharge Agriculture
item.description: Scientists studying the plant have discovered a new way to boost the efficiency of rubisco — the enzyme that powers life on Earth — and hope to transfer the trick to crops.

item.title: Bird Flu Detected in Iowa Backyard Chicken Flocks as Migration Raises Risk
item.description: Backyard chickens are also vulnerable to avian flu, and experts warn that spring migration can accelerate infections across these bird populations.

item.title: Climate Change Could Drastically Cut Grazing Land by End of Century
item.description: The conditions some farm animals thrive under are disappearing, a new modeling study finds.

item.title: Iowa’s High Cancer Rate Linked to Nitrate, Pesticides, PFAS and Radon, New Report Finds
item.description: The new analysis combines science on environmental risk factors with the lived experiences of Iowans battling cancer.

item.title: Can ‘Personhood’ Really Protect Nature?
item.description: The rights-of-nature movement aims to step in where environmental regulations fall short. But some critics are wary of the legal consequences.

item.title: AI Promises Cleaner Farming in Tanzania — and the World. Now Comes the Real Test.
item.description: 53-year-old Roland Daniel Sarikikya is captivated that his mobile phone, which he once used only for calls and texts, can diagnose crop diseases.

item.title: Trump Is Suing to Overturn Prop 12 and Other Animal Welfare Laws
item.description: The administration says animal welfare laws in California are raising egg prices nationwide.

item.title: Silvopasture’s Climate Promise in the U.S. May Be Overhyped, Researchers Say
